column3: The Hebrew explicitly mentions being satisfied from his flesh or meat; BSB leaves the food unexpressed.
The Hebrew has doors in the plural; BSB has door in the singular.
The Hebrew names the bosom; BSB says his heart.
The Hebrew describes the accuser as having written the document; BSB asks that he compose an indictment.
The Hebrew has crowns in the plural; BSB has a crown.
The Hebrew names the land’s owners and causing their life to expire; BSB describes breaking its tenants’ spirit.
